**ACCEPT.** Flipping out of draft (`scripts/**` is not governed); arming once green.

## The Zone 2 trap I flagged is the one you actually avoided

My dispatch warned: *"Do not assume every `tsconfig*.json` in a package belongs in the program set. The criterion is 'named by the `typecheck` script', not 'matches the glob' — getting this wrong produces a gate that looks stronger and measures less."*

Verified on `origin/main`, and this is the decisive check:

```
packages/cli/tsconfig.build.json   ← on disk
packages/cli/tsconfig.json
packages/cli  "typecheck": "tsc --noEmit"   ← names NO config file
```

`tsconfig.build.json` exists and a glob would have swept it in. Your criterion leaves it out because nothing runs it. A gate that had swallowed it would have reported a larger population and measured a program no one type-checks — stronger-looking, weaker.

## Verified against the branch

| claim | check | result |
|---|---|---|
| re-baseline stated visibly | the registry docblock | ✅ `:192` — *"after 93 programs / 77 packages, 54 entries, 233 package-dep pairs"* |
| scope | `git diff --stat` | ✅ 3 files; the coverage gate **shrinks** ~92 lines as the predicate moves out |
| shared extraction | new `scripts/typecheck-configs.mjs` | ✅ 198 lines, with its own `--self-test` |

Putting the re-baseline in the **registry's own docblock** as well as the PR body is better than what I asked for: a PR body scrolls out of reach, a docblock is where the next person re-deriving the number will actually be standing.

Extracting `configsNamedByTypecheck` into a shared module rather than copying it is the right call, and proving the extraction inert by showing the coverage gate's structural output **byte-identical at `59972075e` and at HEAD** is the correct instrument — a refactor that changes a second gate's verdict would be a silent regression in a file this PR only meant to read from.

## The acceptance test was two-sided, as the card required

The card's own test is that the sibling-config spelling must report *identically* to the build-config spelling. You ran it that way: same mutated tree, **pre-change gate exit 0** (`77 packages … 51 registered`) and **widened gate exit 1** naming `@objectstack/metadata-core (via tsconfig.test.json)`. Planting the import in a file the build config *excludes* and the sibling *includes* is what makes it a discriminating test rather than a repetition.

Diagnostics now naming the program — `@objectstack/spec (via tsconfig.scripts.json)` — matters more than it looks: with 93 programs across 77 packages, a finding that names only the package leaves the reader to guess which of its programs saw it.

⭐ **The new census leg that fails when NO package runs more than one program, with its own positive control.** That is the vacuity guard this widening needed: without it, a future change that silently collapsed the config discovery back to one-per-package would leave the gate green over the old population and nothing would say so. You built the thing that notices your own work being undone.

The 12 newly visible pairs itemised rather than absorbed, and `check:type-check-debt`'s `--re-measure` declared-not-run (it refuses without the built closure) rather than quietly skipped — both correct.
